# Licences and provenance

Everything that ships inside `app-debug.apk` is listed here, with where it came from. The short version:

* **All application code is written for this repository.** No source was copied from another project.
* **All bundled media is generated by a script in this repository.** No samples, loops, libraries, fonts,
  textures, models or shaders were downloaded or copied from anywhere.
* **The only third-party code is the dependency list below**, all of it well-known AndroidX/Kotlin libraries
  under the Apache License 2.0, plus JUnit and Hamcrest for tests, which do not ship in the app.

## Application code

`android-app/` — Kotlin sources in `app/src/**`, Gradle build files, the static checkers in `tools/`, and the
six documents in this folder. Written for the Vynyl Record project. The repository has no root `LICENSE`
file, so this document states provenance rather than choosing a licence on the project's behalf; the code is
the project's own and is not encumbered by any third-party source.

Nothing from `android-turntable-native/` (an earlier module in this repository) or from the Next.js web
application was copied into this app: the web app was used as a behavioural reference for the audio chain, the
presets and the copy — the numbers in `VinylRecipe` and the strings in `strings.xml` — and this
implementation is native Kotlin end to end. No React, TypeScript, CSS, API route, Supabase, Cloudflare,
Stripe or middleware code is present, and the web application is untouched by this module.

## Bundled audio

Six files in `app/src/main/assets/audio/`:

| File | What it is | Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bg-guitar.mp3` | a plucked nylon-string figure | ~32 s |
| `bg-cello.mp3` | a bowed, low figure | ~32 s |
| `bg-accordion.mp3` | a reed-like drone with a slow tremolo | ~40 s |
| `bg-rain.mp3` | filtered noise shaped as rain and a room | ~40 s |
| `bg-tape-room.mp3` | tape hum, room tone and a faint mechanism | ~32 s |
| `needle-drop.mp3` | a needle landing in a groove | ~1 s |

**They are synthesised from scratch** — oscillators, envelopes, filtered noise, a Schroeder-style reverb —
by `tools/generate_bundled_assets.py` in this repository:

```bash
python3 tools/generate_bundled_assets.py     # needs numpy and lameenc, development-time only
```

Every file is an original generation of that script; there are no samples, no loops and no recordings of any
kind in them. The script mirrors the *names* of the web application's `public/audio/` files so that a reader
can line the two up, but it does not copy their audio: the bundled versions are generated separately, and are
shorter because they ship inside an APK.

`numpy` and `lameenc` are used **only** by that script. Neither is a dependency of the app, of the Gradle
build, or of the APK; you do not need either of them to build or use Vynyl Record.

## Shaders

`app/src/main/assets/shaders/turntable.vert` and `turntable.frag` are GLSL ES 3.0 written for this project.
They are procedural: no texture, HDRI, environment map or shader from any other source is used or referenced.

## Icon, artwork and images

* The launcher icon is a vector drawable (`ic_launcher_foreground.xml`, `ic_launcher_monochrome.xml`) drawn for
  this project, with an adaptive-icon definition and a monochrome version for themed icons, plus a splash mark
  and a notification icon. There is no raster artwork in the APK at all, which is also why the APK is small.
* Record cover artwork is **generated at render time** by `ArtworkRenderer` from the record's own metadata and
  the chosen vinyl style — the same code draws the label texture on the 3D record. Nothing is bundled.
* The waveform pictures in the library and the player are drawn from the peaks measured from the audio.

## Fonts

No font files are bundled. The app uses the platform's own `Serif`, `SansSerif` and `Monospace` families
through Compose's `FontFamily`, so typography scales with the system, respects the user's font settings and
costs nothing in the APK.

## Tools used to make it, but not shipped

* `tools/kotlincheck.py` — a static checker built on `tree-sitter-kotlin`.
* `tools/check_meshes.py` — verifies mesh winding and normals with `numpy`.
* `tools/generate_bundled_assets.py` — generates the bundled audio (see above).

All three are development tools, run by hand, with their dependencies installed outside the project. None of
them is part of the Gradle build and none of them is in the APK.

## Reporting a problem

If anything in this list is wrong — an asset whose provenance is unclear, a dependency whose licence is
misstated, or code that resembles something it should not — that is a bug worth fixing before anything else.
Open an issue in this repository with the file and the concern.
